identity.title: Measuring the Heating and Cooling of the Interstellar Medium at High Redshift: PAH and [C II] Observations of the Same Star-forming Galaxies at z ∼ 2

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA Band 9 observations targeting [C II] in six $z\sim2$ star-forming galaxies with strong *Spitzer* IRS detections of PAH emission.

distance_source.value: PAH-derived from Spitzer IRS; [C II] line

question.value: How do PAH heating and [C II] cooling compare in the same z~2 star-forming galaxies, as a function of L_IR and IR surface density?

evidence.quote: We compare the properties of PAH and [C II] emission, and constrain their relationship as a function of total infrared luminosity (L$_{\mathrm{IR}}$) and IR surface density.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure PAH redshifts and luminosities from IRS spectra

method.value: MCMC fit of power-law continuum plus Lorentzian (Drude) PAH profiles at 6.2 and 11.3 um; z posterior gives z_IRS; local continuum for luminosities; errors by 1000 Monte Carlo perturbations

evidence.quote: we adopt a simpler model of Lorentzian profiles plus a power-law continuum to fit only the 6.2$\mu$m and 11.3$\mu$m PAH complexes.
This process is repeated 1000 times, after which we quote the standard deviation of all iterations as the $1\sigma$ error.

key_parameters.value: uniform priors on N_pl, alpha, tau, z, b_r

evidence.quote: We assume uniform priors on $N_{pl}$, $\alpha$, $\tau_{\nu,pl}$, $z$ and $b_r$

assumptions.value: Milky Way dust attenuation law; PAH grain properties same as SINGS

evidence.quote: We assume a wavelength-dependent Milky Way dust attenuation law for the optical depth parameter $\tau_{\nu,pl}$
We fit our model (Eq. [\[model\]](#model)) to each *IRS* spectrum using the Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) code `emcee`

analysis_steps.goal: Image ALMA continuum and measure fluxes and sizes

method.value: tclean Briggs continuum imaging; elliptical apertures from 2D Gaussian fit; R_eff,160 from size

evidence.quote: We extracted peak and integrated continuum flux densities through elliptical apertures which were set by fitting a 2D Gaussian function to the bright continuum emission in each observation.
fitting a 2D Gaussian function to the bright continuum emission in each observation

analysis_steps.goal: Detect [C II] and compute line luminosity

method.value: uv continuum subtraction, cube imaging in 30 km/s bins, spectrum from elliptical aperture, integrate line, L_[CII] = 1.04e-3 S dv D_L^2 nu_obs

evidence.quote: We imaged the cube in 30 km s$^{-1}$ bins, and extracted a spectrum through an elliptical aperture
adopt a $\Lambda$CDM cosmology with $\Omega_m=0.3$, $\Omega_\Lambda=0.7$, and $H_0=70$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: Search for lines and set upper limits using redshift-coverage probability

method.value: 0.5'' circular aperture 50 km/s spectra incl. offset apertures, search for three channels >2x rms; compute p(l|ALMA,dz) by integrating z posteriors over spectral window coverage; 3 sigma limit with S dv = 3 dv sqrt(6) rms50, dv=300 km/s
